# The Wolfboyz of Oglah Khan

*Pages PDF 62-71*

## The Wolfboyz • of Oglah Khan
## **A History of Perfidy**
Once, Oglah Khan was one of the Great Hobgobla Khan’s favoured Warlords, a wealthy khan owning several hundred wolves and riders, armed with spear, scimitar, and bow. He was fearsome in battle, his treachery both despised and admired by his fellow Hobgoblins. And yet, even Hobgoblins have a tolerance limit for  perfidy. During the Battle of Xen-Tu, Oglah Khan swiftly switched sides when Hablo Khan was killed by the Dragon Emperor’s champion. Turning on his fellow Hobgoblins as they fled proved a miscalculation when the rest of Hobgobla Khan’s Horde rode over the horizon, massively outnumbering the Cathayans. Declared outlaw, Oglah Khan took the opportunity to leave not just the battlefield, but also the vast eastern steppelands. 

Following a devastating journey through the Dark Lands, where Oglah developed a deep hatred of Chaos Dwarfs, the Wolfboyz joined the Black Orc armies of Gordug Smasher in pillaging Tilea. 

However, Oglah’s treacherous nature emerged again. In the Battle of the Long Knives, Gordug’s Orcs were all but annihilated when Oglah joined Tilean general Giovanni Guilliani. The general, unconcerned by such blatant deceitfulness, rewarded Oglah and his Wolfboyz by hiring them as highly mobile scouts and skirmishers. Since then, Oglah’s Wolfboyz have worked as wolf-riding mercenaries for many princes and generals. 

Their renown has spread throughout Tilea and the Border Princes. The curious thing is this: Oglah has a reputation for treachery, and yet since he first sided with Giovanni Guilliani, there is no recorded instance of Oglah or his Hobgoblins doing anything other than what they were paid to do. What has happened to his legendary treacherous nature? Has he learnt from past mistakes? Does he benefit by working for Tileans more than he did for his previous employers? Or is he biding his time, waiting to make his greatest act of betrayal? 

## **Disposition of the Wolfboyz**
When Oglah left the steppes, over six hundred riders flocked to his cause. Now, barely eighty remain. They travel as a roiling mass with small groups drifting off and wandering about. 

To the untrained eye, they appear a constantly shifting rabble. However, there is a structure. The smaller groups who drift away are satellite outriding parties, remaining within sight of the main group, sharing information as they come and go. Smaller scouting parties venture further forward, out of sight of the rest, spying out the land ahead and watching for ambush. 

## You Can’t Trust Anyone
Oglah has been offered work by a Tilean duce to protect his town from brigands, but he doesn’t trust the man and hasn’t put his X on the contract yet. Oglah wants to know if the duce is honest or trying to pull a fast one, and needs people who can be accepted in town to do some digging. In fact, the duce is honest enough and wants to protect his people. Unfortunately, the brigands are controlled by one of Gordug Smasher’s Black Orcs, a survivor of Oglah’s betrayal at the Battle of Long Knives. The Orc, Barking Ripear, has kidnapped members of the duce’s family, and hopes to use this leverage to lure Oglah into an ambush. 

- Two scouting parties consisting of two or three wolf-mounted Skirmishers. 

## Tempting Treachery

- Two to four outriding parties consisting of 6 to 12 wolf-mounted Skirmishers. Hhrag Wolf-Wispra will be found among them. 

- Sternguard watching the baggage, consisting of 10 Elites and 10 Soldiers. 

- Main force consisting of Oglah (wolf-mounted Chief), “Zschokke” Glahh (wolf-mounted Soldier), Gaglah Ghran (wolf-mounted Elite), 10 wolfmounted Elites, and up to 30 wolf-mounted Skirmishers. 

## **Uniform**
Wolfboy uniforms are a mismatch of clothes and armour from their steppe lives and items scavenged from battlefields. Many of them wear bronze lamellar armour, and helmets surmounted with black wolf tails. 

## **Equipment**
All Wolfboyz are equipped with a spear, a scimitar, and a short bow. Although they’ll scavenge pieces of plate, they prefer scale or light chain. 

## **Shield Design**
Three red talon slashes on a white field. 

## **Battlecry**
‘Hiiyaaarrghh!’ The meaning of the Wolfboyz’ battlecry is obscure, most likely to be offensive and illegal. 

Since his betrayal of Gordug Smasher, Oglah has managed to honour his contracts, defying his reputation. Duce Alphonso wants to change that and persuade Oglah to turn on his current employer, Principessa Gioegia, in the nobles’ upcoming territorial skirmish. Alphonso needs deniable assets, such as the Characters, to do a bit of bribery. If that doesn’t work, can they come up with another way to nobble Oglah’s Wolfboyz? 

## The Pelt of Wulfang
Wulfang was the monstrous steed of Khenghai Khan, the Hobgoblin Empire’s founder. After its demise, the beast’s fur was fashioned into a shoulder mantle and blessed with Waaagh! magic. Gifted to Oglah Khan when he still had the favour of the Hobgobla Khan, the Pelt’s magic grants the wearer +1 _Roughrider_ Talent and their steed +1 M. 

The item is of great cultural value to the Mournguls, and they bitterly resent that Oglah has absconded with the artefact. The Hobgobla Khan has placed a great prize in gold and wolves upon the return of the pelt, and the delivery of Oglah Khan, whom he regards as thief and traitor. Ideally, he would like any would-be bounty hunters to deliver Oglah to him alive, so he can mete out a suitable punishment personally, but should anyone prove able to return either the pelt, or Oglah’s head, they will find the Great Khan appreciative. 

## Olde Weirde’s Incunabulum
We were travelling from Miragliano to Trantio. Somehow, we had found ourselves in the midst of one of the Tileans’ interminable civil wars and had to be at our diplomatic best to avoid upsetting every side at once. Professor von Gronighof’s research had little to do with the political climate, so we were managing to gain access to the historical sources he was after. He claimed that cairns in the foothills of the Appucinis might hold a clue to the fabled skeletal court of Lumbrusco, though this hypothesis has yet to be rigorously tested. 

Shortly after crossing the Tarano river, we were suddenly beset by a number of riders coming from the trees with surprising deftness and speed. At first, I thought they might be Tilean peasant outriders mounted on ponies. But realised they were riding wolves not ponies. And then that they were Greenskins rather than Humans. 

They were dressed partially in Tilean clothing, however, which had contributed to my misapprehension, but also in more exotic garb. Though they were definitely Greenskins, I had never seen their like before, and I could tell from the reactions of my fellow travellers that they were as mystified as I. They were too small and wiry for Orcs, but then too tall and broad for Goblins. I now know, of course, that they are known as Hobgoblins. But I still do not know if that is a type of Goblin or whether the nomenclature is coincidental and erroneous. 

In any case, they rode their wolves very well, in full control of them while wielding their long spears, their blades, or their bows. They were more than a match for us, numbering about a dozen, and circled us menacingly. This could have been the end of our expedition, if they had pressed home their superiority, but I was struck that they were not overly hostile. They seemed to be getting our measure, keeping their distance, but staying within range of their bows. Despite the Greenskin reputation for picking on the weaker foe, I began to suspect that they would not attack. 

However, Sovrissniz did not share my opinion, if she gave the matter any thought at all. She drew her pistols and fired them directly at one of the wolfriders, one shot for the rider and one for the wolf. She hit expertly. Pfaff made a shout of triumph as wolf and rider hit the ground, but I was not so pleased, and I could see Kaia shaking her head. She knew as well as I that Sovrissniz’s volley had signed our death warrant. 

The riders continued to circle but were enraged now by the loss of their comrade and ready to go in for the kill. I waited for the moment when they would loose their arrows and charge, but instead, one of their number rode forward alone. He plainly had some authority over the others. He spat a few words in their guttural language at his subordinates, and they pulled their mounts up and retreated a few paces. I was impressed with how quickly the Greenskin captain was obeyed and how quick they all were to rein in their slobbering beasts. 

The chap (for I call him a chap, though he was plainly a marauding Greenskin) addressed us in broken Tilean. He also displayed a degree of formal courtesy of the sort I thought entirely alien to Goblin-kind. His ettiquete was far from perfect, of course, but it was considerably better than I had seen a good number of aspiring courtiers in Altdorf manage. And although the voice was coarse, the grammar was passable and the vocabulary impressive. He asked us to forgive him for the inconvenience, but his master requested our presence for dinner. This was incredibly magnanimous of the fellow as it was one of his lot who was currently bleeding to death at his feet with one of Sovrissniz’s bullets in him. 

We were escorted to the camp of the local doge. He was plainly in the midst of war with at least one of his neighbouring states. As well as the colourfully dressed local soldiers, there were mercenaries of all sorts. The wealthy Tilean states are famous for the number and variety of mercenaries in their armies. And as we had already discovered, there were apparently Greenskins among them. 

Although I think we were technically prisoners, the doge was most cordial and presented us a with a fine meal. He simply wanted to satisfy himself that we were not spies, or some other threat, and then send us on our way, which he did the next morning with fresh supplies and clean laundry. 

Amongst his keen inquiries of our reason for travelling to Trantio, I could not resist some questions of my own about the wolfriders we had faced. Although my more general observations on warfare in Tilea can be found elsewhere, I will summarise his insights into the Hobgoblins here. 

The doge told us they made remarkably good scouts even though this was not their familiar terrain. In fact, he said they were better than local guides in terms of reliability and cost-effectiveness. A local, he said, is always apt to have other masters, or to simply decide to go home. 

With the Hobgoblins so far from their homelands and without a single ally in all that distance, they were very unlikely to even think about it. 

But more than that, he said the Hobgoblins were masters of deceit upon the battlefield. They were able to ride in such a way that a dozen could kick up enough dust to suggest two hundred riders, and their entire company were able to be so stealthy as to suggest only a dozen. They could flee in the middle of battle looking entirely defeated, but when the enemy broke ranks to pursue them, they would turn instantly and take advantage of the enemy’s confusion. And they could shoot their bows behind them just as well as in front of them, or in any direction, while their mounts were in full gallop. 

They had also perfected a formation whereby as they advance upon the enemy, the front rank shoot their arrows, and then return to the back rank. And by the time it is their turn in the front rank again, they have reloaded, maintaining a withering volley of arrows as they advance. This was easy to describe, but almost impossible to do in practice with any sizeable company. The doge knew, as he had tried to teach his pistoliers the same trick. 

The Hobgoblins’ greatest deceit, however, had occurred when a force of the creatures under the captaincy of one Oglah Khan abruptly changed sides at the Battle of the Long Knives. This gave Giovanni Guilliani, a famous Tilean mercenary general, a stunning victory over a great Orc army. The Hobgoblins seemed to despise other Greenskins and be despised by them in turn. And this, the doge explained, was not the usual petty bickering and powerplay that go on among all their number (and between a good number of Tileans, too, to be fair), but a permanent state of loathing between the Greenskins. 

‘How, then,’ enquired Pfaff, a bit bluntly, but I’m sure we were all thinking along similar lines, ‘can you be sure they will remain loyal to you?’ ‘The thing is,’ the Doge leaned in conspiratorially, ‘Oglah’s perfidy is infamous throughout Tilea and beyond.’ Pfaff nodded. ‘He is now notorious for that betrayal. Everyone who ever hires him will be expecting a betrayal.’ Pfaff nodded again, nonplussed. ‘And we already know that the wolfriders are the masters of the unexpected.’ Nods. ‘So if the Hobgoblins know I am expecting to be betrayed, then I know that is the very last thing that they will consider.’ The doge smiled and tapped the side of his aquiline nose in rhetorical triumph. 

I would like to add to the doge’s observations, here. The discipline displayed by the wolfrider scouts in their encounter with us was exemplary. In spite of our provocation, they were able to stand firm upon their orders; even though we had killed one of their number, they made no move to attack. Notwithstanding the lack of fraternity with which the Greenskins regard their brothers in arms, that is the sort of training and discipline associated with only the best troops. 

But I posit this. The Hobgoblins are hundreds, perhaps thousands, of miles from home, in a strange and belligerent land. They need to play a cagier game here, in Tilea, than they might in their homeland. They are perhaps one bad contract, or one failure, away from destruction, and they have the wherewithal to recognise that. This might be what sets them apart from other breeds of Goblin. 

An Orc would turn on their ally for any slight, real or imagined. That tendency has saved the Empire on more than one occasion, and I am sure that we would be beset by Orc attacks much more regularly if they were able to cooperate better. And Goblins seem instinctively spiteful even when it is not in their best interest. But Hobgoblins, perhaps, are able to see a bigger picture, are able to consider and strategise more proficiently than their green kin. 

Perhaps they are brighter than the other Greenskins and possess more self-discipline, and this is what makes them suitable mercenaries. Instead of considering their next fight and their next meal, as an Orc might, they are able to consider the one after that. And instead of seeking quick and brutal revenge, as a Goblin might, they are about to play a longer game, taking their revenge when it is most advantageous. 

I posited my thoughts to the other scholars but they didn’t seem impressed. Professor Pfaff angrily denied that any form of Greenskin could be anything other than an undisciplined savage, and even when I pointed out that he had witnessed the Hobgoblins exercising stealth, complicated commands, and had kept their composure under hostile fire, he merely denied it and insisted that he remembered things differently. 

Professor Gronighof was reticent to add anything to the conversation, though I later found out he was in the early phases of a bout of Yellow Ague he had contracted from drinking tainted water in Miragliano, and so he was focused on controlling his bowels than contributing to the debate. 

## **Tactics**
Wolfboyz routinely scout their surroundings: whether preparing for battle or travelling, watch for enemies, know the land. Scouts travel singly, in pairs, or trios, dismounting if necessary to avoid observation. Outriders travel in groups of six to a dozen, remaining within sight of the tribe unless they have a specific mission. 

When outnumbering their foe, Wolfboy tactics are simple: ride ‘em down hard, fast, and without mercy. Spears are lowered for a central charge (involving the tribe’s Soldiers and Elites), while flankers (the Skirmishers) contain and harass the enemy with arrows. 

When evenly matched, Wolfboyz seek advantage, striking from ambush en masse or using outrider groups to tempt the enemy into foolishly chasing them into a trap. 

Wolfboyz avoid contracts where they’re outnumbered or outmatched unless they know they have a dagger under their helmets: they’ll cheerfully challenge then flee a mightier cavalry to lead them past the woods where allies have hidden cannons. 

When the tribe sets camp, it’s very busy: tents are erected, blades sharpened, bows fletched, saddles repaired, and wolves (perhaps surprisingly) groomed. However, Wolfboyz also do this in the saddle, even sleeping. 

## Old Scores
During their flight through the Dark Lands, hundreds of Oglah’s infantry spearmen were lost to Chaos Dwarfs, slain or taken as slaves. This still rankles with Oglah. Recently, Oglah has heard rumours of Savage Orcs using hit-and-run tactics to attack Chaos Dwarf caravans and outposts. 

While no lover of Orcs, Oglah wants these rumours investigated to see if he and his Wolfboyz can get a bit of the action. If it means sticking it to the Chaos Dwarfs and maybe saving some of his own ladz they enslaved, he’ll grit his teeth and work with a buncha Orcses. If the Characters fancy an expedition to the Dark Lands, Oglah will fund it and offer one of his skirmishers as a guide. 

## **Down in the Woods**
## **Easy Encounter**
Passing through a woodland clearing or skirting a forest’s edge, the Characters hear sounds of something large crashing through the bushes and trees. It’s heading towards them. They have a Round to react. 

A giant, wild-eyed wolf emerges, leaves and twigs caught in its fur, a loose saddle half falling off. Surprised by the Characters’ presence, it checks its flight. If they managed to hide, perhaps up a tree, it still stops, suddenly uncertain at the clearing or open space beyond the forest. 

If the Characters attack, the wolf fights. Intimidation might scare it into flight or a stand-off; failure leads to violence. If the Characters don’t react within a Round, the creature bounds off. It’s possible the Characters keep the wolf at bay and uncertain, especially if they use Skills like Charm Animal or Animal Care. 

Three Rounds after the wolf ’s arrival (sooner if it’s held at bay), a pair of mounted Hobgoblins emerge from the woods in pursuit of the errant wolf. 

If the Characters are holding the wolf at bay without attacking, the Hobgoblins position themselves to help contain the wolf without panicking it. They’ll bark orders to the Characters to help them in this. One of the Hobgoblins gets down from his wolf to calm the creature and reset its saddle. Neither Hobgoblin is hostile towards the Characters unless attacked. 

Shortly, a battered Hobgoblin hobbles from the wood to wincingly remount his steed. If the Characters, Hobgoblins, and wolves end up fighting, this Hobgoblin arrives two Rounds into the fight, stays hidden, and uses his bow. 

If the encounter resolves peacefully, one Hobgoblin grunts and tosses the Characters a dagger with a wolf paw handle. 

This encounter consists of: 

- A loose Giant Wolf. 

- Two Hobgoblin Skirmishers on Giant Wolves. 

- One Hobgoblin Skirmisher on foot. 

## **Damage Limitation Medium Encounter**
This encounter involves an outrider group from the main tribe. The Hobgoblins are Elites, and may even be Oglah Khan and his bodyguard. There are six to twelve in the group, whatever is required to give the Characters a stiff fight. The challenge is greater if the Characters are on foot (see **WFRP** , page 163, and **Up in Arms** , page 105, for more on mounted combat). 

If you want to avoid mounted combat, have the encounter involve Wolfboy spearmen travelling alongside one of the tribe’s baggage wagons. The spearmen (mostly Elites) outnumber the Characters, making combat a risky proposition. 

The conflict stems from a resource that the Hobgoblins want, but which is being denied them: access to a water supply on someone’s land; a farmer’s crop to feed themselves and the rest of the warband; a barn to rest the night; the right to enter a small town owned by the Wolfboyz’ current employer. 

There are two ways to begin this. One is where the war of words is over just before the Characters arrive on the scene, and first fists have flow. Can the Characters very quickly deescalate the situation or do they get stuck into a difficult fight without further thought? They shouldn’t expect much help in a fight; the only other people involved might be a poor farmer and his wife and children, for example. 

Alternatively, the Characters can be involved from the start and have an opportunity to bargain with the Hobgoblins when they first appear on the scene. The Hobgoblins are not automatically violent, and can be reasoned with to find a mutually agreeable settlement. It’s worth remembering that the Wolfboyz are successful mercenaries and they have access to gold and other resources. However, because they scare people, hardly anyone actually considers trading with them. 

This encounter consists of: 

- Six Hobgoblin Elites on Giant Wolves. 

- Either Oglah Khan or Gaglah Ghran on Giant Wolves. 

## **Signed in Blood Hard Encounter**
The Characters are hired by a party with an invested interest in seeing Oglah Khan’s Wolfboyz performing at a suboptimum level in an upcoming battle. The party in question wants them to somehow infiltrate the Wolfboyz’ camp and do whatever they can to achieve this, perhaps by dosing the wolves’ meat with laxatives (the Hobgoblins’ too), cutting and weakening saddle straps, or sewing doubt. Alternatively, placing caltrops or other traps in the warband’s path or knobbling scouts before they can report back. 

Any of this puts the Characters in direct conflict and likely close proximity with the entire warband. Precise numbers are somewhat irrelevant, as even if the Characters are discretely taking out scouts, sooner or later they’ll have larger groups of outriders on their backs, and eventually the entire warband will come calling. Unless the Characters are the stuff of legend, they’re likely stuffed. At best, they’ll be captured after a game of catand-mouse. 

Oglah Khan will want a word with them. He’ll ask a simple question: did they sign a contract? If they did, he’ll expect them to honour it, and if they try turn traitor on their employer, he’ll be unimpressed. Either way, they’ll find themselves in a pit with some hungry wolves. If they put up a decent fight and survive, they’ll be sent packing with a boot up the arse and a warning not to do it again. 

However, if they didn’t sign a contract, Oglah considers treachery entirely acceptable. He offers them the chance to switch sides and work for him. He’ll make them sign a contract though, with their blood. Heaven help them if they betray him. 

## A Greater Betrayal
Why have the Wolfboyz apparently abandoned their treacherous ways in favour of working for Tilean mercenary commanders with a degree of professionalism? Perhaps Oglah really has just worked out that Humans won’t stand for too much mischief from the Hobgoblins. Perhaps there is a grander treachery afoot, and the wolfboyz are merely acting as scouts for their first employer, the Hobgoblah Khan. If this is the case, the Wolfboyz are merely the advance scouts of a much larger force of Hobgoblins intent on sweeping across the Old World as a conquering force. 

## **Oglah Khan – Hobgoblin Chief**
Oglah is an imposing figure, with an air of restrained psychopathy. He shows an unnerving, gruff courtesy towards Humans and Halflings (Human children in his eyes). However, he stands tall and proud and looks princes in the eye without deference, knowing he’s at least their equal on or off the battlefield. If obliged to behave diplomatically, he avoids Dwarfs as they often react violently. However, if they can resist outright hostility, he can tolerate their passive aggressiveness. Oglah is fascinated by Elven archery skills and bows; Elves themselves unnerve him, leaving him curiously reticent. 

In and out of battle, Oglah is constantly looking for advantage over the enemy. His treacherous nature usually focused against those he’s contracted to fight. Something people haven’t realised is that since becoming a mercenary, Oglah has to sign contracts, which he does with an X in his blood. He takes this with superstitious seriousness.

## **“Zschokke” Glahh – Hobgoblin Soldier**
“Zschokke” Glahh has become an enthusiast for all things Tilean. He has adopted the demeanour and style of what he imagines is a roguish Tilean general, and taken a Tilean name he considers suitable for a Hobgoblin. He wears a felt hat with a big feather and a colourful but stained sash, offset with ill-matched armour and homemade medals. While not the strongest of the tribe, his eccentricity has been met with suspicion from his fellow Wolfboyz. He also unnerves many Tileans he encounters, something he remains completely oblivious to. 

Zschokke has never been afraid of battle, but his experience of Tilean bravado has added a hasty recklessness to his actions and even a glimmer of honour. If there’s any Wolfboy likely to find himself involved in a duel or riding to the rescue of a fair principessa (who certainly won’t appreciate being rescued by a Hobogblin, even if she finds herself in significant peril), it’ll be Zschokke.

## **Gaglah Ghran – Hobgoblin Elite**
Gaglah Ghran is a big, angry, and formidable Hobgoblin, who favours his heavy-bladed spear over his scimitar. He’s one of a handful of Wolfboyz who’s unhappy about leaving the steppes and has not assimilated well to his new life. However, he’s kept his opinions to himself for the most part, although some are aware of his feelings. This includes Oglah, who has considered promoting Gaglah to the ranks of his personal bodyguard (as much as to keep a wary eye on him as to benefit from his protection). 

Gaglah refuses to replace his old amour and weapons, which while heavily dented and battered, remain vicious. His grey wolf ’s fur cloak is extremely dirty and ragged. These are all precious mementoes of a lost life; their theft or loss are certain to provoke him to reckless fury. If there is any Wolfboy likely to betray Oglah Khan or punch “Zschokke” Glahh in the head, its Gaglah. He’s something of a ticking timebomb, but perhaps Oglah can keep him under control if he is vigilant enough.

## **Hhrag Wolf-Wispra – Hobgoblin Skirmisher**
Hhrag has a way with wolves. He can get even the most troublesome of beasts to lay down and beg. Many assume this is because wolves are smart enough to take notice of his heavy wolfskin cloak, decorated with wolf tails, wolf paws, and necklaces of fangs. The truth is entirely the opposite, however: wolves just love him, and he never treats them badly, despite his marked tendency to collect their body parts. 

Because he spends so much time with them, often sleeping alongside them, Hhrag possesses a certain… aroma. It’s that strong, even other Wolfboyz notice it and he’s rarely used for scouting missions that require staying beneath notice. However, Oglah finds him very useful if offensive diplomacy is needed, as he tends to make opposing generals terribly uncomfortable and distracted. The prospect of being overrun by Hobgoblins who smell as bad as Hhrag might encourage a quick surrender.
